title: Evidence-Anchored Overdose Death Prediction from Death Investigation Reports
abstract: arXiv:2610.19556v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Confirmation of overdose deaths in the United States is often delayed due to the complexities of certifying drug-involved deaths. Death investigation reports represent a rich but underutilized data source that could be used to predict whether a death is a suspected overdose (i.e., a death preliminarily identified as an overdose prior to the final cause and manner of death determination). We present an automated framework that classifies suspected overdoses from death investigation reports, while producing supporting explanations guided by expert knowledge. Through an expert-guided design process, we investigate 1) what type of explanations are best for model prediction performance, and 2) which architecture is better suited for this task: pipeline models that rationalize first and then predict, or self-rationalizing models that jointly predict and rationalize? translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.19556v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：在美国，由于涉及药物死亡的认证过程复杂，药物过量死亡的确认常常被延误。死亡调查报告是一种丰富但未被充分利用的数据源，可用于预测某例死亡是否为疑似药物过量（即在最终死因和死亡方式判定之前被初步认定为药物过量的死亡）。我们提出了一个自动化框架，能够从死亡调查报告中对疑似药物过量死亡进行分类，同时生成由专家知识引导的支持性解释。通过专家引导的设计过程，我们研究了以下两个问题：1）哪种类型的解释最有利于提升模型预测性能；2）哪种架构更适合该任务：是先进行合理化解释再预测的流水线模型，还是将预测与合理化解释联合进行的自我合理化模型？我们的实验表明，采用基于证据锚定的解释流水线模型（原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个从死亡调查报告中预测疑似药物过量死亡的自动化框架，通过专家引导生成证据锚定的解释，并比较了流水线模型与自我合理化模型在该任务上的性能差异。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an automated framework that predicts suspected overdose deaths from death investigation reports with expert-guided, evidence-anchored explanations, and compares whether pipeline models or self-rationalizing models perform better for this task.
